taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.note: By eye from the photos (observations 3770337, 148080836, 328974622, 69283601, 10776079, 346930362, 21148131, 45087852): a coarse, bushy clump of stiff, felty grey-green culms, short rigid blades, and narrow straw-coloured spikes of bearded spikelet groups. The panicle's colour is set by hand (spikes pale straw, sRGB 215, 205, 170 by eye from the photos (the sources read give no colour)), as no colour character applies to a spikelet and flower_colour, which the family's rule reads, is a flower's; its spikelets come from the order's rules. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Pleuraphis rigida: a native perennial grass, highly branched at the base, giving it a bush-like appearance.

traits.woodiness.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: plants rather robust at base, branching, the base rather woody, decumbent or rhizomatous.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: culms numerous, rigid, felty-pubescent, 50 to 100 cm tall; FEIS: 12 to 40 inches (30-100 cm).

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: culms 50 to 100 cm tall; FEIS: 30-100 cm.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: FEIS species review, Pleuraphis rigida: its clumped growth form is a result of the tillers or short rhizomes it produces.

traits.clonal.note: FEIS species review, Pleuraphis rigida: tillers or short rhizomes.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: blades spreading, 2 to 5 cm long, or longer on sterile shoots.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: blades 2 to 4 mm wide, more or less involute, acuminate into a rigid coriaceous point.

traits.inflorescence.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: group of spikelets about 8 mm long, densely bearded at base, the groups along a spike.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: spikes 5 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 468, Hilaria rigida: group of spikelets about 8 mm long.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a grain (caryopsis), as in every grass.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS species review, Pleuraphis rigida: flowers from February through September in Arizona; Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 130): February to September.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: grains ripe April to October, after each flush of flowers.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for big galleta from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.7 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

traits.culm_branching.note: Hitchcock (1935, p. 468), Hilaria rigida: plants rather robust at base, branching, the branches mostly erect or ascending; FEIS: highly branched at the base, giving it a bush-like appearance.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
